title: Targeted in utero electroporation of the ventro-temporal mouse retina
protocol: Prepare a solution of Xylazine/Ketamine diluted in sterile 0.9% NaCl.
Warm the Xylazine/Ketamine solution on the heating pad.
Prepare a solution of buprenorphine diluted in sterile 0.9% NaCl.
Warm the buprenorphine solution on the heating pad.
Anesthetize the timed-pregnant mouse via an intra-peritoneal injection of Xylazine/Ketamine solution (10 mg·kg−1 and 100 mg·kg−1, respectively).
Alternatively, use gas anesthesia with isofluorane for faster recovery.
Inject subcutaneously the anesthetized mouse with the analgesic buprenorphine solution (0.0125 mg·kg−1).
Insert the needle in the middle of the abdomen between the lower nipples at a depth of about 6 mm.
Perform the intraperitoneal injection with the needle at 45° to the skin to avoid damaging the embryos.
Cut the tip of a capillary to 0.5 mm maximum using Dumont forceps.
Obtain a beveled tip on the capillary.
Fill the capillary with DNA solution using a mouth aspirator tube.
Use a microinjector for filling the capillary if available.
Ensure the capillary tip is sharp and thin but not too thin to avoid clogging.
Verify that the capillary is not clogged by ejecting some DNA solution.
Prepare the mouse for surgery.
Shave the lower part of the mouse abdomen using a hair trimmer.
Disinfect the shaved area first with povidone iodine, then 70% ethanol.
Place a gauze pad on top of the shaved abdomen as a surgical drape.
Wet the gauze pad with warmed 0.9% NaCl (30°C) using a Pasteur pipette to adhere it to the skin.
Perform a midline laparotomy by making a longitudinal incision approximately 1.5 cm long through the linea alba.
Cut the skin first, then cut the muscle without going past the lower nipples.
Expose the uterine horns after cutting as straight as possible for easy suturing and scarring.
Very gently pull one uterine horn out of the abdomen cavity, by grabbing it between embryos.
Keep all embryos wet throughout the surgery using warm and sterile 0.9% NaCl delivered with a Pasteur pipette.
Inject DNA into the eye during the procedure.
Gently grab the first embryo with standard forceps and immobilize it.
Position the embryo so the eye is in close apposition to the amniotic membrane and uterine wall.
Pierce the uterine wall, amniotic sac, and eye using a capillary filled with DNA solution.
Inject 1 μL of DNA solution into the eye using the capillary almost parallel to the uterine wall.
Electroporate the retina after injection.
Immerse the electrodes in highly conductive ultrasound transmission gel.
Place the head of the embryo between the electrodes, approaching the paddles from the back.
Place the negative electrode on the ventro-temporal part of the injected eye.
Place the positive electrode on the opposite side of the head.
Adjust the angle between the electrode and the head axis so that the ventro-temporal retina is between the cathode and anode.
Apply five electric pulses of 45 V for 50 ms every 950 ms using the paddle of the preprogrammed electroporator.
Wet all embryos profusely with warm, sterile 0.9% NaCl after electroporation of each embryo.
Avoid any damage to the placenta during manipulation and injection through blood vessels.
Gently hold the embryos with minimal force during electroporation.
Repeat steps for all embryos.
Repeat these steps for embryos in the second uterine horn.
Assess survival rate by noting total number of electroporated embryos.
Start electroporation from the embryo closest to the ovary and proceed in order.
Gently place the uterine horns back in the abdominal cavity.
Fill the abdomen with warm and sterile NaCl 0.9%.
Close the muscle with continuous sutures.
Close the skin with lock-stitch sutures.
Apply oxybuprocaine as a local anesthetic if the mouse endures pain during suturing.
Apply povidone iodine to the sutures.
Place the mouse in an incubator at 30°C until it wakes up before returning it to its cage.
Do not clean the cage for at least two days before and five days after surgery.
Leave the embryos to develop normally.
Minimize disturbances to the mouse during the first 48 hours post-surgery.
Check for signs of pain such as a hunched position, reduced activity, or squinted eyes.
Inject an analgesic solution (0.0125 mg·kg−1 buprenorphine) if signs of pain are detected.
Proceed to euthanasia if the analgesia does not improve mouse welfare.
Carefully check for suture integrity until the skin is properly closed.
Re-suture if necessary, although repeated anesthesia can be detrimental to embryo survival.
Dissect the retina to assess electroporation efficiency.
Image the dissected retina to confirm cell labeling in the VT region.
Make a longer incision in the ventral retina for orientation purposes.
Dissect and image the optic chiasm to validate RGC targeting.
Visualize projections of electroporated RGCs at the optic chiasm level.
Examine brain targets in both ipsilateral and contralateral hemispheres.
